notes: This is the polite form of the Japanese copula. It is used at the end of a sentence to state that something exists, is a certain way, or is a specific noun.
Unlike English 'to be', it does not change based on who the subject is (I, you, they, etc.).
It is usually attached to the end of a noun or na-adjective. For i-adjectives, it is often added after the adjective's root form.
